originalTitle: Optimal blocker matching on one ghost path
originalStatement: A ghost path with e edges and k available blocker vertices has maximum matching size min(e,k).
originalHypotheses: Canonical positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and the named banked lemmas in the source.
independence: Proof reconstructed from primary arguments and explicit definitions. Earlier source status/review assertions were not treated as proof. The author previously collected these sources; the present derivations and finite/exact-algebra checks are new independent audit work.
detailedDerivation: A path v0→…→ve has e candidate ghost edges, and k available endpoint vertices. Capacity one on edges and vertices bounds every matching by min(e,k).
If all e+1 vertices are available, assign each edge to its target, obtaining e matches.

Otherwise choose a nonavailable vj. Assign every available vi with i<j to edge i and every available vi with i>j to edge i−1. On either side edge indexes are distinct, and the two sets are disjoint, so all k available vertices are saturated.

There are e+1−k nonavailable vertices, hence unmatched edge count max(0,e−k)=max(0,r−1). An available non-source vertex is exactly a surviving mortal echo owner, since q<σ_a<d(a)<d(q) gives its actual blocker service.

Owner-only matching already uses every available target. The source gains one additional match precisely when it is available and some target is unavailable. This proves μ=L+T and the stated U,V,Q formulas, without any asymptotic assertion.
